title: Sayyid Dynasty
capsule: The Sayyid dynasty was the fourth ruling house of the Delhi Sultanate, founded by Khizr Khan in 1414 after he captured Delhi as a nominal governor for the Timurid ruler Shah Rukh. Khizr Khan claimed descent from the Prophet Muhammad (hence 'Sayyid'), though this genealogy was disputed; he and his successors Mubarak Shah, Muhammad Shah, and Ala-ud-Din Alam Shah ruled over a greatly reduced sultanate hemmed in by regional powers in Bengal, Gujarat, and the Deccan. The last ruler, Alam Shah, abdicated voluntarily in 1451 in favour of Bahlul Lodi, transferring power without conflict and ending the dynasty after thirty-seven years of weakened but continuous rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty's territorial extent was limited and shrinking; the borders of effective Delhi Sultanate control under the Sayyids are documented in chronicles but are known to have been loose, with much of the nominal territory held only intermittently.
